source: Original room paintings and passageway cutouts generated for this project from its authored room descriptions and recorded prompts. No outside image pack, franchise illustration, named-artist style, logo, font, music or real-person likeness reference was supplied.
rights_note: AI-assisted project artwork, subject to the applicable service terms. This record does not guarantee uniqueness, copyrightability, exclusive ownership, or comprehensive legal clearance. It does not select a whole-project license or change the independent SRD and software permissions.
processing: Original generated PNG files are retained unchanged in assets/rooms. Runtime uses the standard library to extract exact atlas cells, crop/resize backgrounds, and scale alpha-aware passage cutouts; no runtime image-library dependency. Separate dynamic enemies, hands, loot, documents and portals remain independent of the paintings. Rear-passage placements are authored in each painting's coordinates and projected through the same viewport crop; large foreground fixtures can intentionally obscure a far passage without changing dungeon navigation.

atlases.prompt: Create one ORIGINAL game environment art atlas, a perfectly SQUARE large PNG contact sheet. STRICT LAYOUT: exactly TWO equal columns and SIX equal rows, TWELVE separate rectangular landscape scenes. Each tile is 3:1 wide, all tiles aligned to the exact equal grid edge-to-edge, NO margins, NO gutters, NO borders, NO captions, NO panel numbers. This is a 2D first-person dark fantasy dungeon game background atlas, original realistic physically based environment concept art with rich weathered materials, convincing lighting and depth. Every tile is a DIFFERENT chamber. The viewer stands inside each chamber at human eye height, wide horizontal view, floor visible in lower third, environment in upper two thirds. Keep the central lower/middle standing area clear for a separately rendered enemy; place unique room landmarks to the sides and rear, still large/readable. No adventurer, no first-person hands, no monsters, no living people, no bosses, no weapons floating in foreground, no HUD/UI, no actual written words/letters/logos/watermark. Inscriptions and documents are atmospheric illegible marks, never readable text. Do not add treasure chests, gold piles, potion bottles or collectible gear unless the description explicitly calls for a decorative object, because loot will be drawn separately. Use sealed/dark walls at the far center and peripheral blank stone wall zones for separately drawn actual passageway overlays; do not invent extra open exits. Any described portal is CLOSED/inactive; any described guardian is omitted but keep its architecture. All twelve scenes should remain clearly visible and distinct, not blended across tile boundaries. No copying franchise art or named artist style. FLOOR ATMOSPHERE: moonlit upper burial catacombs; gray worn limestone, dusty blue moonlight and warm lantern fill; solemn royal tombs. EXACT TILE ORDER, row by row left to right then next row. Each entry gives its landmark and exact atmosphere to depict (do not print these titles): Row 1, LEFT: The Broken Stair. Moonlight spills down a cracked stairway. Your first dungeon awaits: reach Thalinor's inner chamber and defeat its warden to prove yourself. | Row 1, RIGHT: Hall of Whispering Kings. Broken statues watch from the shadows. Your footsteps stir whispers from mouths carved in stone. | Row 2, LEFT: The Rootbound Vault. Pale roots push through the ceiling, winding around empty stone coffins like the fingers of a giant hand. | Row 2, RIGHT: Chapel of the Last Light. A silver altar catches the glow of your lantern. The candles around it have been cold for centuries. | Row 3, LEFT: The Sunken Gallery. Dark water fills the grooves between flagstones. Torn banners cling to the walls above a forgotten battlefield mural. | Row 3, RIGHT: The Ashen Armory. Rusting weapon racks line the walls. Beneath the dust, a few old runes still flicker with stubborn light. | Row 4, LEFT: The Scribe's Tomb. Fragments of parchment cover a stone desk. A faded inscription lists the names of adventurers who once completed this trial. | Row 4, RIGHT: The Echoing Well. A dry well opens in the center of the chamber. Every sound returns from its depths a heartbeat too late. | Row 5, LEFT: The Hall of Chains. Heavy chains hang from the ceiling. They sway despite the still air, clicking softly against one another. | Row 5, RIGHT: The Pilgrim's Refuge. A stone bench and a shattered waterskin mark an old resting place. Someone scratched a tiny sun into the wall. | Row 6, LEFT: The Starless Observatory. A collapsed dome reveals only solid rock. Tarnished bronze rings once tracked stars that Thalinor no longer sees. | Row 6, RIGHT: The Warden's Sanctum. Blue fire surrounds the throne of the upper tombs. The Warden raises its blade before a sealed arch. Beyond it, roots strain against the stone; this guardian protects the first threshold, not the end of the catacombs.

panels.name: The First Foundation
panels.description: The earliest builders' tools lie sealed within transparent stone. Their unfinished inscription asks the city's heart to protect all who will live above.

panels.name: The Coronation Grave
panels.description: A royal procession is carved around an empty sarcophagus. The king's likeness has no face, and every carved witness turns away from him.

panels.name: The Chamber of the Offering
panels.description: A stone bowl rests on an altar beneath the royal seal. A single dried handprint marks where the king offered his heart to halt the disaster.

panels.name: The Blackwater Court
panels.description: Dark water covers the floor of an abandoned audience hall. Ripples gather toward an empty dais, as if unseen courtiers still kneel there.

panels.name: The Crown's Shadow
panels.description: A broken crown is painted above a doorway. Its shadow falls across your path even when your lantern points in the opposite direction.

panels.name: The City's Memory
panels.description: Small belongings fill shelves cut into the rock: a child's cup, a mason's cord, a gardener's knife. These are the lives the king meant to save.

panels.name: The Last Chain
panels.description: The final intact restraint crosses the chamber at chest height. Its links strain with each heartbeat from the throne, shedding silver dust.

panels.name: The Nameless Choir
panels.description: Cracks in the walls carry hundreds of thin voices. For a moment they speak together: he gave his heart, but it was never enough.

panels.name: The Sealed Dawn
panels.description: A golden mosaic shows sunlight falling over Thalinor before its ruin. Beneath it, a narrow passage exhales cold air from the royal chamber.

panels.name: The Heartless Antechamber
panels.description: The heartbeat grows loud enough to drown your breathing. An inscription beside the throne door names the man the king once was, before the stone beneath it turns black.

panels.name: The Hollow Throne
panels.description: The city's foundations curve around a throne carved from its own bedrock. The Hollow King rises beneath a fractured crown, an open darkness where his heart should be. All the catacombs' chains lead here.

doorways.prompt: NEW ORIGINAL GAME-ART ASSET: a PORTRAIT 1024x1536 transparent PNG atlas, exactly THREE equal columns and FIVE equal rows, fifteen separate architectural doorway cutouts. No gutters, captions, borders, text, labels or checkerboard. True transparent ALPHA everywhere outside each doorway frame, including between cells. Every doorway entirely fits its own cell with 8% transparent padding and no overlap. These are realistic textured OPEN PASSAGEWAYS for compositing into first-person dungeon room paintings, not flat icons or UI panels. Each aperture has an OPAQUE near-black tunnel interior with subtle realistic depth and a few worn threshold stones; only the outside beyond each stone/iron/root frame is transparent. Tall arch or lintel, convincing thick weathered jambs, dark recess, soft contact shadows limited closely to frame, rich physically plausible detailed materials, no broad rectangular wall or background plate. No closed door leaf, no knobs, no writing, no people, no creatures, no foreground hands/weapons. In EVERY row: LEFT COLUMN is a passage in the left wall viewed obliquely from room center (left foreground jamb larger, far/right jamb recedes), CENTER COLUMN is a straight-on arch on a distant rear wall, RIGHT COLUMN is a right-wall passage viewed obliquely (mirror of the left view). The standing floor edge aligns at each cell bottom, eye-level camera. Exactly one complete opening in each cell. Five ROWS correspond to these lighting/material themes in order: ROW1 pale gray cold limestone royal catacombs, crumbling carved stone, faint blue moonlight and gentle warm lantern rim. ROW2 buried root grove, dark damp mossy green stone, thick pale twisting roots round the jambs, tiny amber sap highlights. ROW3 Ashen Forge, riveted soot-black iron reinforcement over rough dark stone, muted copper fittings and restrained orange furnace rim glow. ROW4 Starless Vault, dark indigo black marble, restrained silver reinforcement and cold violet-blue reflected light, elegant severe ancient prison architecture. ROW5 royal foundations, weathered rose-black bedrock, subtle tarnished gold royal relief motifs, warm dim reddish reflections and dark damp stone. Make the stone frames blend naturally into corresponding realistic environment paintings, irregular softened outer silhouettes, no bright uniform outline. Original generic dark fantasy designs, no franchise imagery or outside artist style.
doorways.layout: Rows: floors 1–5. Columns: left-wall passage, front passage, right-wall passage. Transparent exterior and dark tunnel interiors; only actual known exits are drawn.

packaging: All six room/passage PNG assets and this provenance record are embedded byte-for-byte in the desktop executable and verified. The release also includes a readable copy as legal/room-artwork-sources.json; exact file hashes appear in build-manifest.json.
